disposition_reason: Reports per-sample Pb, Ni, Cd and total Cr (flame AAS) in 30 locally made "chocolate" products bought in Lahore, with descriptive statistics. Products are mostly compound or filled chocolate-flavoured confectionery, many without listed cocoa, and the data have multiple internal unit and range inconsistencies, so values are low-reliability and of marginal scope for the cocoa page.

study.material_scope: locally manufactured chocolate and chocolate-flavoured confectionery (bars, balls, biscuits, cream, liquid chocolate, toffee, cones, coconut-filled)
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Purchase market: local shops and departmental stores, Lahore, Pakistan; products manufactured by Pakistani companies (Lahore, Karachi, Faisalabad, Hub, Sahiwal). Cocoa origin not reported.
study.sampling_unit: individual retail products (one per brand), analysed in triplicate
study.method: Flame AAS (PerkinElmer AAnalyst 800, air-acetylene, D2 background correction) after aqua regia digestion; sample mass and digest volume not reported
study.basis: not stated; reported as ppm (mg/kg) of product
study.qa: Calibration with blank and triplicate standards; no recovery, CRM or LOD reported.

findings.material: Locally available chocolate products (mostly compound/filled confectionery)
findings.basis: not stated (finished product as purchased presumed; "ppm" derived from digest mg/L x 50)
findings.notes: All 30 locally manufactured "chocolate" products from Lahore shops; Table 1 shows they are mostly compound/filled confectionery (coconut-filled, chocolate biscuits, cream, liquid chocolate, toffee, cones, sticks) with vegetable fat; 12 of 30 list no cocoa ingredient at all. Not plain chocolate. No sample mass, LOD/LOQ, recovery or CRM reported; "ppm" = digest mg/L x 50 with an unexplained footnote "Concentration in grams x 100 mL".
findings.integrity_issue: Abstract and Table 2 give range 0.375-3.4 mg/kg but the Discussion states the highest Pb was 3.75 mg/kg.

exceedance_notes: Authors: Pb 27/30 above 0.5 mg/kg (2 equal, 1 below); Ni 24/30 above 0.025 (2 equal, 4 below); Cd 16/30 above 1.0 (3 equal, 11 below); Cr 16/30 above 0.02 (2 equal, 12 below). Recount from Tables 2-5 reproduces these counts.
contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary calls the products "finished chocolate" and "direct chocolate occurrence evidence"; Table 1 shows mostly compound/filled confectionery with vegetable fat, and 12 of 30 products list no cocoa ingredient.

Stored summary does not flag the inconsistent mg/L-to-ppm factors in Table 3 (Ni: CBCBCB-8, KC-23, MMLC-25) and Table 5 (Cr: KC-23), the Discussion Pb maximum of 3.75 mg/kg, or the Discussion Cr maximum of 0.085 mg/kg.
Stored summary says "triplicate analysis for each chocolate sample" as fact; the tables only label "Triplicate each sample" and report a single mean digest concentration without dispersion.
unresolved: Sample mass and digest volume are not stated, so the x50 mg/L-to-mg/kg conversion (footnote "Concentration in grams x 100 mL") cannot be verified.
Collection period not reported (paper received February 2021).
Whether results are on as-sold basis is not stated.
Cocoa content of the products is not reported; which products are real chocolate versus cocoa-free compound confectionery can only be inferred from Table 1 ingredient lists.

Cd values of 0.5-3.5 mg/kg in products with little or no cocoa are implausible relative to cocoa-content-driven Cd; cannot determine whether this reflects contamination, calibration error or unit error.
